parsed.explanation: No criminalisation, a comprehensive Gender Equality Act 2019 covering gender identity across all spheres, a judicial conduct code, and a state sensitisisation programme for officials form a protective framework in force. No traveller-facing exposure is documented anywhere: no border/document friction, no facility restriction, no police targeting, no violence record. The 2015 report found no LGBT-specific abuses; an openly operating LGBTIQ initiative signals social acceptance. Dated and thin, however: enforcement of the Act is not shown operating, and entry screening, detention placement, facilities and care access are simply undocumented open questions. Absence of evidence is not safety, but structural signals are positive.

entry_documents.exposure: No document-marker, visa or airport-screening rule or incident documented either way.
entry_documents.protection: No criminalisation; Gender Equality Act 2019 bars indirect as well as direct discrimination across all spheres, including services.
entry_documents.interaction: Not documented whether border officers apply the Act or rely on unstated document checks.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: 2015 report flagged general prison conditions and corruption, but recorded no torture, arbitrary detention or disappearances.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Judicial conduct code bars bias; no trans-specific custody practice documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Custody placement rules for outed visitors are not addressed; would interact with any document mismatch.

federal_state_facilities.interaction: Dossier states no subnational variation; any island or settlement differences remain unevidenced expectation only.

care_services.exposure: Not documented — the dossier explicitly contains no data on gender-affirming care access or refusal.
care_services.protection: Gender Equality Act covers provision of goods and services, which would in principle reach clinics.
care_services.interaction: Emergency-care or ward treatment of an outed visitor is an open question, not a documented harm.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No threat-framing of trans people documented; no trans-specific hostility in law or statements.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Act obliges government to eliminate stereotypes and prejudice and to sensitise judicial, law enforcement and public officials; Code of Judicial Conduct 2008 binds judges and lawyers.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Sensitisation programme's actual reach at frontline border or street encounters is undocumented.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented for visiting families; marriage non-recognition and s.428 ages are resident-facing, not visitor exposures.
minors_guardians.protection: Equal age of consent (16) regardless of sex or orientation removes differential treatment.
minors_guardians.interaction: No documented rule on how a minor's documents or gender presentation would be handled at entry.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented anti-trans street violence or police abuse; 2015 report listed no LGBT-specific abuses (dated evidence).
street_violence_police_response.protection: Openly led LGBTIQ initiative, youth ambassador and summit representation indicate documented social acceptance; Act bars discrimination in the social sphere.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Foreigner status versus local treatment of gender-nonconforming people is not separately addressed.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Enforcement of the 2019 Act is not shown operating; court backlog or police non-compliance undocumented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Supreme Court functioning and pending constitutional question indicate accessible institutions; Act creates government obligations and judicial sensitisation.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unknowns concern application, not existence, of recourse; open questions are lighter than documented exposures.

anchor_checks.comparison: Far above. Vellandra imposes a universal, routinely enforced exclusion register with no remedy — a state-directed traveller-facing exclusion. This dossier documents no entry restriction, no registration, no denial mechanism of any kind, and instead an in-force equality statute. The gap is tier: known universal exposure versus none documented.

Above. Kestrel Isles has documented secondary screening, discretionary refusal of entry and slow remedies — real, evidenced traveller friction. Here no screening practice or refusal is recorded at all; the only uncertainty is undocumented absence, and the statutory framework points positively. This dossier lacks the evidenced administrative holds that place 0.55 there.

Slightly above. Meridia documents trained border staff, an equality statute and tribunal appeals — but also actual brief detention and humiliating secondary screening. This dossier has comparable formal machinery plus documented social acceptance, and zero documented adverse incidents, so it sits a notch higher despite thinner enforcement proof.

Below. Norathia shows protections operating: specialist training, body cameras, a tribunal ordering release and apology, airlines accepting chosen names. Here the protections are documented as enacted but not shown operating, and no traveller-specific procedure (entry, screening, care) is evidenced at all — hence 0.79 rather than 0.85.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime for a visitor is: no criminalisation, an in-force anti-discrimination statute reaching gender identity in services and social spheres, judicial conduct rules, and an official sensitisation programme for law enforcement — a framework with no documented traveller-facing restriction layered on top of it. Documented social acceptance (openly operating LGBTIQ initiative, youth diplomacy) reinforces this. The rating stops short of the 0.85+ tier because enforcement is unproven, the anti-abuse evidence is a decade old, and every traveller-specific axis — border documents, detention placement, facilities, care, minors — is an open question rather than an assessed exposure. For an adult alone or with a minor, nothing in the dossier threatens discovery consequences; residual risk is bureaucratic and unknown, not hostile.
